core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Diabetic Osteomyelitis is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Plan for Diabetic Osteomyelitis: Bone biopsy and culture, prolonged IV antibiotics, surgical debridement, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: non-healing deep foot ulcer probing to bone

Key HPI features: A 77-year-old male presents to the clinic with non-healing deep foot ulcer probing to bone. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: Temp 37.6C, HR 88, BP 138/82. Deep plantar ulcer over the first metatarsal head with visible bone at the base, positive probe-to-bone test, surrounding erythema and mild cellulitis. Diminished sensation to 10g monofilament testing, diminished pedal pulses. ESR 78 mm/hr, CRP elevated. Plain foot X-ray shows cortical erosion and periosteal reaction of the first metatarsal; MRI confirms bone marrow edema consistent with osteomyelitis.
Relevant background/PMH: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus diagnosed 15 years ago, complicated by peripheral neuropathy and peripheral arterial disease; hypertension.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Diabetic Osteomyelitis.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Cellulitis alone (no bone involvement) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Systemic signs of infection (fever) — suggests spreading infection.
management_principles: Plan for Diabetic Osteomyelitis: Bone biopsy and culture, prolonged IV antibiotics, surgical debridement
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective:
Chief Complaint: non-healing deep foot ulcer probing to bone

A 77-year-old male with a 15-year history of type 2 diabetes complicated by peripheral neuropathy presents to the clinic with a non-healing deep foot ulcer probing to bone. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: Temp 37.6C, HR 88, BP 138/82. Deep plantar ulcer over the first metatarsal head with visible bone at the base, positive probe-to-bone test, surrounding erythema and mild cellulitis. Diminished sensation to 10g monofilament testing, diminished pedal pulses. ESR 78 mm/hr, CRP elevated. Plain foot X-ray shows cortical erosion and periosteal reaction of the first metatarsal; MRI confirms bone marrow edema consistent with osteomyelitis.
reference_soap.assessment: Diabetic (foot ulcer-associated) Osteomyelitis of the first metatarsal, supported by a positive probe-to-bone test, elevated inflammatory markers, and MRI findings, in a patient with longstanding diabetic neuropathy and peripheral arterial disease.
reference_soap.plan: Assess severity, perfusion, and need for urgent drainage; obtain plain films and MRI when needed. Obtain deep tissue or bone culture when feasible before antibiotics if this will not delay necessary treatment. Use culture-directed antibiotics by oral or IV route according to severity and bioavailability, and involve wound-care, vascular, infectious-disease, and surgical teams for selective debridement or revascularization.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Diabetic Osteomyelitis
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Diabetic Osteomyelitis
Implement evidence-based management plan: Bone biopsy and culture, prolonged IV antibiotics, surgical debridement

teaching.one_liner: A chronic bone infection arising from a non-healing diabetic foot ulcer that has progressed deep enough to probe to bone.
red_flags: Systemic signs of infection (fever) — suggests spreading infection

must_ask.say: How long has this ulcer been there without healing?
Has a doctor ever probed this wound down to the bone?
How well controlled is your diabetes?
Can you feel your foot normally, or has it gone numb?
Any fever or feeling generally unwell?
